instruction: Initiate returns via FedEx for everything in my last 4 amazon order.
notes: Single-app task (amazon) plus supervisor. Flow: get passwords -> amazon login -> show_orders (identify the 4 most recent orders) -> show_order for each to learn its items (product_id, quantity) -> show_return_deliverers to find FedEx's id -> initiate_return for every item of every order with the item's full quantity -> complete_task (no answer). Item counts per order are unknown at modeling time, so the problem instantiates one placeholder product/quantity pair per order; at runtime amazon-initiate-return is executed once per order_items entry of each order (the eval checks the full order->product->quantity map). Order composition (in-order, item-quantity) is static structure in :init; knowledge gating is done by orders-listed, order-details-known and deliverers-listed. Because the domain cannot reference problem objects, supervisor-complete-task takes the four returned products and the deliverer as non-API parameters with pairwise inequality, so its precondition is exactly the goal conjunction. Side-effect changes to gmail/file_system records are produced automatically by initiate_return and are not modeled.
